title: Nimbus TV Box requires firmware refresh
symptoms: Picture freezes after a few minutes
Streaming apps take unusually long to start
Audio drops out intermittently
Channel lineup changes disappear
Remote control shows no response when navigating menus

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the box displaying the latest software version in Settings > About?
Do other devices on the same network stream without issues?

steps.text: Ask the customer to navigate to Settings > System > Software Update on the Nimbus TV Box.
Verify that the box reports 'Checking for updates…' and then shows an available version newer than the current one.
Instruct the customer to select 'Download and Install'. Confirm that the progress bar appears and the box remains powered throughout.
After installation, the box will reboot automatically; ensure the customer sees the Nimbus splash screen and the home UI loads.
Return to Settings > About and confirm the version number matches the latest release note (e.g., 3.2.1).
Ask the customer to launch a streaming app and verify playback is smooth for at least 5 minutes.
Document the update in the ticket and close if performance is restored.

escalate_when: Update fails to download or install
Box reboots continuously after update attempt
Symptoms persist after confirming latest firmware
notes: Firmware updates address known stability bugs and security patches. Ensure the box stays powered via wall outlet during the process; do not advise power cycling as primary fix.
root_cause: set-top box needs a firmware update

title: Intermittent playback on Nimbus TV Box due to weak line
symptoms: Video pauses for several seconds then resumes
Screen freezes while audio keeps playing
Streaming stops after a few minutes of watching
Other apps on the box lag or stutter

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the TV box connected to the network via Ethernet cable?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Advise to connect with Ethernet and retest

diagnostic_questions.q: Do any other devices on the same network show similar video stalls?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Focus on the TV box configuration

steps.text: Log into the Nimbus Service Portal and run the Line Quality Test for the customer's feed; record signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and attenuation values.
If SNR is below 30 dB or attenuation exceeds 45 dB, schedule a line inspection or recommend a cable replacement.
Inspect the coaxial cable from the wall outlet to the TV box for visible damage, kinks, or loose connectors; reseat or replace the cable with a certified RG-6 segment.
On the Nimbus TV Box, navigate to Settings → Network → Advanced and perform a manual DNS flush, then re-apply the network profile.
Check for pending firmware on the TV box (Settings → System → Software Update) and apply the latest version if available.
After hardware and firmware actions, run a 5-minute playback test of a high-bitrate stream and verify that pauses no longer occur.

escalate_when: Line Quality Test remains below threshold after cable replacement
Playback still stalls after all steps and multiple devices are affected
notes: Document all measured line metrics and cable serial numbers in the ticket. If escalation is required, attach the Line Quality Test report and any photos of the inspected cabling.
root_cause: buffering caused by a weak line

title: Streaming app login failure on Nimbus TV Box
symptoms: The app shows a blank screen after I type my credentials
I receive an "Unable to verify account" message
It keeps prompting me for my password even though it's correct
My favorite channels refuse to open and display an error icon

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the Nimbus TV Box showing a solid internet indicator (green Wi-Fi or Ethernet icon)?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask customer to verify network connection

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer recently changed their Nimbus account password?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Advise to update password in the app

steps.text: Confirm the TV box is obtaining a valid IP address; navigate to Settings → Network and verify "Connected" status. Expected: IP address displayed and connection status green.
Check system date and time under Settings → General → Date & Time; ensure they are correct and set to automatic. Expected: Accurate date/time shown.
Clear the app cache: go to Settings → Apps → [Streaming App] → Storage → Clear Cache. Expected: Cache cleared confirmation.
Force-close and relaunch the app. Expected: App restarts and proceeds to credential screen.
Re-enter the Nimbus account credentials, making sure to use the exact email and password. Expected: Credentials accepted and home screen loads.
If the app still rejects credentials, delete the app data (Settings → Apps → [Streaming App] → Storage → Clear Data) and sign in again. Expected: Fresh app state, login screen appears.
Verify that the account is not locked by checking the Nimbus web portal on a separate device. Expected: Account status shows "Active".
If all above succeed, perform a soft reboot of the TV box (Menu → Power → Restart). Expected: Device restarts and app loads without error.

escalate_when: Error code 401 or similar authentication error remains after step 8
Customer reports the same issue on multiple devices
Account appears locked or disabled in the portal
notes: Do not advise a full factory reset unless instructed by Tier 2. Document any error codes shown by the app.

title: Remote Control Not Paired with Nimbus TV Box
symptoms: Handheld controller does nothing when buttons are pressed
Channel changes fail to register
Volume adjustments have no effect
Power button on the TV box does not respond to the controller
On-screen navigation menus ignore input

diagnostic_questions.q: Are the controller's batteries fresh and inserted correctly?
Is there a clear line of sight between the controller and the TV box's IR sensor?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Remove obstacles and ensure the sensor is not covered

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the controller been paired with this TV box before?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Attempt to re-pair using the menu

steps.text: Ask the customer to power-cycle the TV box by unplugging it for 10 seconds, then plug it back in; confirm the box boots to the home screen.
Instruct the customer to open the Settings menu, navigate to 'Accessories', and select 'Add New Controller' - the box should display a pairing prompt.

Tell the customer to locate the pairing button on the back of the controller (usually a small recessed button), press and hold it for 5 seconds until the LED blinks, then confirm the box detects the device.
If detection fails, have the customer remove any infrared-blocking objects, ensure the controller is pointed directly at the sensor, and repeat step 3.
Once the controller appears in the list, have the customer select it and confirm pairing; the box should show a 'Pairing successful' message.
Ask the customer to test basic functions (power, volume, channel) to verify responsiveness.
If the controller still does not respond, guide the customer to perform a factory reset of the controller by holding the pairing button for 15 seconds, then repeat steps 2-6.
Document the outcome in the ticket and advise the customer to keep spare batteries handy for future issues.

escalate_when: Controller remains unresponsive after two pairing attempts
Box reports a hardware fault on the IR sensor
Multiple controllers fail to pair with the same TV box
notes: Ensure the customer does not have a universal remote programmed to the box, as it can interfere with the pairing process. If the issue persists after all steps, a hardware replacement of the IR receiver module may be required.

title: Unexpected SIM Change - Nimbus Mobile
symptoms: I stopped getting my two-factor authentication codes via text
My device shows as inactive while another phone is listed as my primary
I'm seeing a sudden increase in my monthly data usage
Calls and messages are being routed to a different number
I can't access my online account because verification goes to an unknown phone

diagnostic_questions.q: Did you recently request a new SIM card or change your device?
Are you receiving verification codes on a phone you don't recognize?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Flag as potential fraud and follow the remediation steps
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Check account activity logs for anomalies

diagnostic_questions.q: Has your account password been changed without your action?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Treat as possible account takeover and escalate

steps.text: Confirm the caller's identity using at least two pre-registered security questions and an OTP sent to a previously verified channel; outcome - identity verified or not
Open the Nimbus Mobile provisioning console and pull the recent SIM-change audit trail for the account; outcome - see timestamp and source of SIM change
Cross-reference the audit entry with the customer's answer from step 1; if the change was not authorised, mark it as unauthorized; outcome - classification of the event
Immediately place a temporary lock on the account and issue a block command for the newly provisioned SIM in the network management system; outcome - the rogue SIM cannot be used for calls or data
Log the incident in the Fraud Management System, attach all audit screenshots, and schedule a follow-up call within 48 hours; outcome - case documented and closure path defined

escalate_when: Customer cannot verify identity through standard channels
The unauthorized SIM change occurred within the last 24 hours and high-value services are at risk
Multiple fraudulent transactions are detected on the account
notes: All actions must be recorded in the case file. Do not share any personal data outside the secured Nimbus systems. If the customer reports loss of the original device, initiate the lost-device workflow in parallel.
root_cause: SIM swap without the customer's consent

title: Handling Unauthorized Fibre Plan Modifications
symptoms: my monthly bill is higher than usual
the internet speed shown in my app is different
I see a new service added to my account I never requested
I got a notification about a plan upgrade I didn't approve

diagnostic_questions.q: Did you receive any email or SMS confirming a plan change?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to verify the change details and source, then continue troubleshooting
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask if they have shared account credentials recently

diagnostic_questions.q: Have you noticed any login to your Nimbus account from an unfamiliar device or location?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Document the login event and treat as potential takeover

steps.text: Verify the caller's identity using the standard KYC script (full name, address, last 4 digits of the account number, and security question).
Access the account management console and pull the recent activity log for the last 48 hours, focusing on plan modification events and login timestamps.
If a plan change event is present, note the timestamp, the operator who performed it, and the source IP/device. Compare it against the customer's known devices.
Revert the plan to the original tier using the 'Rollback Plan' function; capture the confirmation ID and send a summary to the customer via secure email.
Reset the account password, enforce a new strong password, and enable two-factor authentication. Record the reset transaction in the case file.
Place a temporary hold on any further plan modifications for 24 hours, and schedule a follow-up call to confirm the account remains unchanged.

escalate_when: the customer cannot answer the KYC questions or verification fails
multiple unauthorized changes are detected within a 24-hour window
notes: Document all actions in the CRM audit trail. Use internal reference code SF-UNAUTH-PLAN for future reporting.

title: Unexpected International Activity Detected on Nimbus Mobile
symptoms: My bill shows charges from countries I've never visited.
I received alerts about data consumption while I was at home.
There are outgoing calls in my record that I didn't make.
I got a message saying my phone is connected to a foreign network.

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer recently traveled outside their home country?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Proceed to investigate possible account compromise.

diagnostic_questions.q: Are there recent SIM change requests or new device activations on the account?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Verify the legitimacy of the change.

steps.text: Confirm the customer's identity using KYC checks (DOB, address, last-4 of payment method).
Retrieve the account's roaming log for the last 30 days and note any foreign network connections.
Match flagged charges against the roaming log; highlight any entries without a corresponding travel record.
Temporarily suspend international voice and data services on the line while the investigation proceeds.
Force a reset of the account PIN/password and require the customer to set new security questions.
Order a replacement SIM, deactivate the old ICCID, activate the new SIM, and record the change in the fraud case file.

escalate_when: If foreign charges remain after the SIM replacement and service suspension.
If the customer cannot confirm their identity through standard verification.
notes: All actions must be logged in the fraud management system and comply with data-protection regulations. Notify the security team if the case is escalated.

title: Customer reports unexpected account changes after receiving a suspicious text
symptoms: I got a message saying my account was locked and asked for my password
My login no longer works and I'm asked to verify my identity
I see new devices or numbers linked to my account I didn't add
I received a call asking for my account details and now something changed

diagnostic_questions.q: Did the customer click any link or reply to a message requesting personal details?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to verify account ownership; suspect credential compromise

diagnostic_questions.q: Is there any recent SIM change or number-port request on the account?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Treat as potential SIM swap; follow SIM-swap protocol

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer noticed unfamiliar charges or service modifications?

steps.text: Confirm the caller's identity using pre-registered security questions and the account PIN
Access the Nimbus Fibre admin console and pull the audit log for the last 48 hours to identify password, contact-detail, or device-registration changes
If unauthorized changes are found, revert them to the original values and place a temporary lock on the account to prevent further edits
Force a password reset and enable mandatory multi-factor authentication for the portal login
Remove any newly added device IDs or SIM profiles and generate a fresh secure authentication token for the customer
Send a secure in-app notification confirming the corrective actions and provide guidance on recognizing fraudulent communications
Add a fraud-alert flag to the account and schedule a follow-up review within 48 hours
Record all actions in the case notes, update the incident log, and close the ticket if no further anomalies appear

escalate_when: Customer cannot verify identity using known security factors
Unauthorized SIM or number-port change is detected
Evidence of broader account compromise beyond password reset
notes: This procedure addresses phishing-style messages that trick users into revealing credentials. It does not replace the standard SIM-swap workflow but adds extra checks for credential-based attacks targeting Nimbus Fibre customers.
